mission_2.observations: I think the most important observed behaviors are how the participant reacted to giving commands and then being met with confirmation but confirming too late. This seemed to be an annoyance for the participant because they felt as if they didn't have enough time to read and respond. As time went on the reaction time became faster because they became accustomed to it, but this is a way to show how one can also be trained by a machine and its not always a person training a machine. I also noticed this myself when completing earlier tasks. Starting off was relatively annoying because I thought I would have more time to confirm before it stopped and disregarded that command.
mission_2.breakdown: Predictability is interesting here because something becomes predictable when you have seen something enough times before. At first the confirmation wasn't completely predictable to the participant because they assumed that after the command the robot would just complete the task. But after seeing that the first time it became predictable for future commands. The way the display screen shows this also help in its predictability because if there was no display then the user would have no idea what is happening and that would make it completely unpredictable.
mission_2.limits: It can be concluded that someone who has never used this system is able to give commands to a robot however it can't be concluded that this approach is the best and most transparent and safe for the real world. While it may be something that anyone can give commands to, it is specific to one scenario and doesn't really provide how it would interact in other environments.
